goal: Distinguish this debugger-only access violation from an app crash and point to the XAML Hot Reload in-app toolbar workaround.
must_include: Uses the debugger-only timing and `.vs` setting to suspect the XAML Hot Reload in-app toolbar overlay.
Recommends disabling only the in-app toolbar option while keeping XAML Hot Reload itself enabled if desired.
Mentions that this was a Windows App SDK 1.4 / Visual Studio 17.7-era tooling/runtime interaction and should be retested after updating Visual Studio and Windows App SDK.
Treats the crash as a native access violation in Microsoft UI/windowing code, so normal managed exception handlers will not make it safe to continue.
must_not: Tell the developer to remove their second window or rewrite the app as a single-window app.
Suggest adding a broad `try/catch` around window activation as the fix for the access violation.
Recommend disabling all debugging or all XAML Hot Reload before trying the narrower toolbar setting.
acceptable_alternatives: Temporarily disable XAML Hot Reload entirely if the toolbar-specific setting is unavailable.
Upgrade Visual Studio and the Windows App SDK, then re-enable the toolbar to verify whether the crash is fixed.
solved: The answer identifies the in-app XAML Hot Reload toolbar as the likely trigger and gives the disable-toolbar/update-and-retest path.
partial: The answer recognizes a native Visual Studio/debugger/tooling interaction but does not name the in-app toolbar setting.
notes: The scenario intentionally baits an app-code investigation; the fixture points to Visual Studio Hot Reload settings instead.
